Formulation  
Patrick Smith, a 35-year-old lawyer, presents with a cluster of somatic and psychological symptoms (headaches, palpitations, shortness of breath, tingling, reduced appetite, loss of libido) temporally associated with a recent job change and sustained occupational stress. Underlying hyperthyroidism is managed with thyroxine, but further investigation of thyroid function and somatic symptoms is required. Anxiety is the likely contributing factor to the somatic complaints and reduced libido. Protective factors include insight and willingness to engage in further assessment.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Anxiety with somatic symptoms  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce frequency and severity of headaches, palpitations, and anxiety symptoms; improve appetite and libido  
- Clinical Goal(s): Conduct thorough clinical assessment including physical examination and relevant blood tests to rule out organic causes; establish diagnosis; initiate appropriate management  
- Actions (Patient): Attend scheduled in-person clinic appointment for examination and investigations; report any worsening symptoms promptly  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Perform physical examination including cardiovascular and respiratory assessment; order relevant blood tests including thyroid function; assess for comorbid anxiety or other mental health conditions; coordinate further mental health support as indicated  

Secondary Problem: Reduced appetite with unintentional weight loss  
- Patient Goal(s): Regain normal appetite and stabilize weight  
- Clinical Goal(s): Identify cause of appetite loss; monitor weight and nutritional status; support hydration and nutrition  
- Actions (Patient): Monitor appetite and weight changes; maintain food intake as able  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Review nutritional status; provide advice or refer to dietitian if indicated  

Tertiary Problem: Loss of libido  
- Patient Goal(s): Restore sexual function and libido  
- Clinical Goal(s): Assess contributing psychological and physiological factors; address underlying anxiety and medical causes  
- Actions (Patient): Discuss concerns openly during consultations  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Evaluate for endocrine or psychological causes; consider referral to specialist if appropriate  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Relationship between stress/anxiety and physical symptoms; importance of attendance for examination and investigations  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increase in headache frequency, palpitations, worsening breathlessness, anxiety escalation  
- Coping Strategies: Not recorded
